config.title: Test Context

intro.title: Test Context
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React application that uses the Context API to share a theme (like 'light' or 'dark') across multiple components without passing props manually. You'll learn how to create a context, provide its value from a parent component, and consume it in child components using the useContext hook. The main technologies involved are React, TypeScript, and the Context API, which helps manage global state efficiently. By the end, you'll understand how context simplifies data sharing in a React app, making your code cleaner and more maintainable.
intro.usecase: Testing React Context is essential for building maintainable applications with shared state, such as user authentication systems where login status must be accessible across components. In e-commerce platforms, shopping cart state needs to be consistently tested to ensure items persist correctly across pages like product listings and checkout. Dashboard applications rely on tested context for theme switching (light/dark mode) and user preferences that affect multiple UI panels simultaneously. Developers implement context tests to prevent state-related bugs in complex features like multi-step forms, real-time notifications, or language localization systems.

objectives: Initialize a React Context with TypeScript types
Construct a Context Provider component to wrap application sections
Implement a custom hook to consume context values
Configure components to subscribe to context updates
Apply context to share state across multiple components
Update context values through provider callbacks
Render components that dynamically respond to context changes

steps.title: Import React, createContext, useContext, and useState
steps.instruction: Import React, createContext, useContext, and useState from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use a single import statement or multiple import statements to bring in all four APIs from 'react'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing multiple React APIs
import React, { useState, useEffect } from 'react';
steps.seedCode: // Import React, createContext, useContext, and useState from 'react'
steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary React APIs are imported and ready to be used in your component.
successCriteria: React, createContext, useContext, and useState are all imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You imported some of the required APIs, but not all. Make sure to import React, createContext, useContext, and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are incorrect or missing. You need to import React, createContext, useContext, and useState from 'react'.

steps.title: Define the context type interface
steps.instruction: Define a TypeScript interface named 'MessageContextType' with two properties: 'message' of type string and 'setMessage' of type React.Dispatch<React.SetStateAction<string>>.
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and property definitions inside curly braces.
steps.seedCode:
// Import React, createContext, useContext, and useState from 'react'

// Define the MessageContextType interface here
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a TypeScript interface that defines the shape of the context value, which will be used when creating the context.
successCriteria: The MessageContextType interface is defined with 'message' (string) and 'setMessage' (React.Dispatch<React.SetStateAction<string>>) properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure both properties are included with the correct TypeScript types.
steps.feedbackWrong: The interface definition doesn't match what's needed. Check that you have both 'message' and 'setMessage' properties with the correct types.

steps.title: Create the context with default values
steps.instruction: Create a context using createContext with default values matching the MessageContextType interface. Name it MessageContext.
steps.hint: Call createContext with an initial value object that matches your interface properties.
steps.analogousExample:
// Creating a context with default values
const ThemeContext = createContext({ theme: 'light', toggleTheme: () => {} });
steps.expectedOutcome: A MessageContext constant is created using createContext with appropriate default values.
successCriteria: MessageContext is created using createContext with an object containing message and setMessage properties matching the interface.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your context includes both message and setMessage properties with appropriate default values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The context wasn't created correctly. Remember to use createContext with an object matching the MessageContextType interface.

steps.title: Create the provider component
steps.instruction: Define a functional component named MessageProvider that accepts children as props and returns them wrapped in the context provider.
steps.hint: Create a component that takes children as a prop and uses the MessageContext.Provider to wrap them.
steps.expectedOutcome: A MessageProvider component is created that will wrap its children with the context provider.
successCriteria: MessageProvider is defined as a functional component that accepts children as props and returns MessageContext.Provider wrapping the children.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the provider component, but make sure it accepts children as props and returns the MessageContext.Provider wrapping them.
steps.feedbackWrong: The provider component isn't defined correctly. It should be a functional component named MessageProvider that accepts children and returns them wrapped in MessageContext.Provider.

steps.title: Initialize state in the provider
steps.instruction: Inside the MessageProvider component, use useState to initialize a state variable called 'message' with an initial value of 'Hello from context!'.
steps.hint: Call useState inside the component body, before the return statement. The state variable should be typed as string.
steps.expectedOutcome: The provider component now has a state variable 'message' initialized with the string 'Hello from context!'.
successCriteria: The MessageProvider component contains a useState call that declares a state variable named 'message' with the initial value 'Hello from context!'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState with the correct initial value and variable name.
steps.feedbackWrong: The state initialization is missing or incorrect. Use useState to create a 'message' state variable with the initial value 'Hello from context!'.

steps.title: Define the provider value object
steps.instruction: Inside the MessageProvider component, create a value object that contains the message state value and the setMessage function.
steps.hint: You can define a constant called 'value' that holds an object with 'message' and 'setMessage' properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: The provider component now has a value object ready to be passed to the context provider.
successCriteria: A value object is defined inside MessageProvider with 'message' and 'setMessage' properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your value object includes both 'message' and 'setMessage' properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try creating a value object with the message state and setMessage function inside the MessageProvider component.

steps.title: Wrap children with the provider
steps.instruction: Inside the MessageProvider component, wrap the children prop with the MessageContext.Provider component.
steps.hint: The provider should return the MessageContext.Provider JSX element with the children prop placed inside it.
steps.expectedOutcome: The MessageProvider component now returns the provider JSX structure with children properly wrapped.
successCriteria: The MessageProvider component returns MessageContext.Provider with the children prop inside.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the provider returns the MessageContext.Provider JSX element with {children} inside it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The provider component should return the MessageContext.Provider with children wrapped inside.

steps.title: Create a consumer component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named MessageDisplay that will consume the context value using useContext.
steps.hint: Define a component that uses useContext(MessageContext) to access the message and setMessage values.
steps.expectedOutcome: A MessageDisplay component is defined that will consume the context values.
successCriteria: The MessageDisplay component is defined and uses useContext(MessageContext) to access context values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a component, but make sure it uses useContext(MessageContext) to access the context values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The MessageDisplay component isn't defined correctly. Create a functional component that uses useContext to access MessageContext.

steps.title: Consume context in the consumer component
steps.instruction: Inside the MessageDisplay component, call useContext with MessageContext to get the context value.
steps.hint: Use the useContext hook with the MessageContext object as its argument.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: consuming context in a component
const value = useContext(MyContext);
steps.expectedOutcome: The MessageDisplay component will have access to the context value via useContext.
successCriteria: useContext is called with MessageContext inside the MessageDisplay component.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're calling useContext with the MessageContext object as its argument.
steps.feedbackWrong: The MessageDisplay component should call useContext with MessageContext to get the context value.

steps.title: Display context data and add update button
steps.instruction: In the MessageDisplay component, return JSX that displays the current message from context and a button that updates it when clicked.
steps.hint: Use the message value from context in a paragraph or heading, and call setMessage in the button's onClick handler with a new string.
steps.expectedOutcome: The MessageDisplay component will render the current message and a button that updates it, demonstrating how to consume and update context values.
successCriteria: MessageDisplay returns JSX containing the message value and a button with an onClick handler that calls setMessage.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're both displaying the message value and providing a button that calls setMessage when clicked.
steps.feedbackWrong: The MessageDisplay component doesn't yet display the message or include an update button. Review how to consume context and trigger updates.
